With an open-jaw ticket (into Narita/NRT and out of Kansai/KIX), you have a linear route that minimizes backtracking. A **Tokyo → Kyoto → Hiroshima day trip → Osaka** route is achievable at a moderate pace, as the high-speed Shinkansen makes cross-city travel seamless.

---

### Key Vegan Survival Notes for Japan
* **Hidden Ingredients:** Traditional *dashi* (fish stock) is omnipresent, even in seemingly vegetarian dishes like miso soup, tofu dressings, and noodle broths. Bonito flakes (*katsuobushi*) are also widely used.
* **Essential App:** Download **HappyCow** before you land. It is the gold standard for navigating plant-based food in Japan.
* **Helpful Phrase:**  
  * *"Watashi wa bīgan desu. Dashi, niku, sakana, tamago, nyūseihin wa taberaremasen."*  
  (I am vegan. I cannot eat fish stock, meat, fish, eggs, or dairy.)
* **Convenience Store (Konbini) Backups:** Plain salted rice balls (*shio-musubi*), edamame, roasted sweet potato (*yaki-imo*), bananas, and plain soy milk.

---

### Trip Overview
* **Day 1 (Oct 1):** Arrive NRT → Tokyo (Historic Asakusa & Ueno)
* **Day 2 (Oct 2):** Modern Tokyo (Meiji Shrine & Shibuya)
* **Day 3 (Oct 3):** Shinkansen to Kyoto (Fushimi Inari & Gion)
* **Day 4 (Oct 4):** Classic Kyoto (Arashiyama & Buddhist Shojin Ryori)
* **Day 5 (Oct 5):** Hiroshima & Miyajima Day Trip → Base in Osaka
* **Day 6 (Oct 6):** Osaka (Osaka Castle & Dotonbori)
* **Day 7 (Oct 7):** Retro Osaka (Nakazakicho/Umeda) → Late Departure from KIX

---

### Detailed Itinerary

#### Day 1 (Oct 1): Welcome to Tokyo (Tradition & Recovery)
* **Morning:** Land at NRT at 06:00. Clear customs, grab an IC transit card (Suica/Pasmo) on your phone or at the station, and take the **Narita Express (N'EX)** or **Keisei Skyliner** into Tokyo. Drop luggage at your hotel (Asakusa or Ginza areas work well).
* **Afternoon:** Stroll through **Senso-ji**, Tokyo’s oldest temple in Asakusa. Walk along Nakamise-dori shopping street (look for freshly made plain *senbei* / rice crackers). 
* **Evening:** Take a relaxed walk along the Sumida River toward Tokyo Skytree.
* **Vegan Eats:**
  * *Lunch/Dinner:* **T’s Tantan** (inside major stations like Ueno or Tokyo Station) — famous 100% vegan ramen and gyoza.
  * *Alternative:* **Gonpachi Asakusa Azabujuban** (offers a dedicated, clearly labeled vegan menu).

#### Day 2 (Oct 2): Modern Tokyo & Green Escapes
* **Morning:** Start early at **Meiji Jingu Shrine**, nestled in a tranquil forest in the center of the city.
* **Afternoon:** Walk through **Harajuku** (Takeshita Street) and head down to **Shibuya**. Experience the famous **Shibuya Crossing** and take in views from the **Shibuya Sky** observation deck (book tickets 4 weeks ahead).
* **Evening:** Explore the neon alleys of Shinjuku or relax in Shibuya.
* **Vegan Eats:**
  * *Lunch:* **2foods** (Shibuya LOFT) — creative plant-based fast-casual comfort food and donuts.
  * *Dinner:* **Vegan Ramen UZU Tokyo** (near Toyosu, teamLab-themed dining) or **Afuri Ramen** (multiple locations; ask for the dedicated "Hazelnut Vegan Ramen").

#### Day 3 (Oct 3): Tokyo to Kyoto (Shrines & Lanterns)
* **Morning:** Board the morning Tokaido Shinkansen (approx. 2h 15m) to Kyoto. Drop luggage at your hotel (stay near Kyoto Station or Downtown Karasuma/Shijo).
* **Afternoon:** Take a short train to **Fushimi Inari Taisha**. Visiting in mid-to-late afternoon means fewer crowds and a cooler hike through the thousands of vermilion torii gates.
* **Evening:** Head to the historic **Gion** district and stroll along **Pontocho Alley**, an atmospheric canal-side street lit by lanterns.
* **Vegan Eats:**
  * *Dinner:* **Engine Ramen** (offers rich vegan ramen broths) or **Ain Soph. Journey Kyoto** (fully plant-based, famous for fluffy vegan pancakes and savory sets).

#### Day 4 (Oct 4): Timeless Kyoto & Buddhist Cuisine
* **Morning:** Visit **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** early (around 07:30–08:00) before tour groups arrive. Visit the UNESCO-listed **Tenryu-ji Temple** right next to the grove.
* **Lunch:** **Shigetsu** (inside Tenryu-ji). Experience *Shojin Ryori*—traditional Zen Buddhist vegetarian cuisine, inherently vegan, made with seasonal plants, tofu, and sea vegetables. *(Advance reservation required).*
* **Afternoon:** Head east to explore **Kiyomizu-dera Temple** and walk down the preserved cobblestone streets of Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka.
* **Evening:** Relaxed evening near the Kamo River.
* **Vegan Eats:**
  * *Dinner:* **TowZen** (specializes in plant-based soy-milk ramen in a cozy traditional setting) or **Mumokuteki Cafe** (popular plant-based cafe in downtown Kyoto).

#### Day 5 (Oct 5): Day Trip to Hiroshima & Miyajima → Move to Osaka
* **Morning:** Forward your main bags to Osaka via hotel luggage delivery (*Takkyubin*), or take an early morning Shinkansen from Kyoto with your bags, switch trains at Shin-Osaka, and store luggage in a locker at Hiroshima Station. 
  * Take the scenic ferry to **Miyajima** to see the famous "Floating" Torii gate of **Itsukushima Shrine** and friendly wild deer.
* **Afternoon:** Return to Hiroshima city. Visit the **Peace Memorial Park & Museum** and the **Atomic Bomb Dome**—a moving, essential historical visit.
* **Evening:** Catch the Shinkansen to **Osaka** (approx. 1h 20m) and check into your hotel (Namba or Umeda areas).
* **Vegan Eats:**
  * *Lunch in Hiroshima:* **Nagataya** (near Peace Park; offers a dedicated vegetarian/vegan okonomiyaki cooked on separate grill surfaces with vegan sauce).
  * *Dinner in Osaka:* **Oko - Fun Okonomiyaki Bar** in Shinsaibashi (quirky, friendly spot with customizable vegan okonomiyaki).

#### Day 6 (Oct 6): Osaka’s Flavor and Vibrancy
* **Morning:** Explore the grounds of **Osaka Castle** and its outer park.
* **Afternoon:** Head to the trendy **Orange Street (Tachibana-dori)** in Minami for vintage boutiques, record shops, and third-wave coffee shops.
* **Evening:** Explore **Dotonbori** to experience Osaka’s legendary neon lights, the Glico Running Man sign, and the buzzing entertainment district.
* **Vegan Eats:**
  * *Lunch:* **Paprika Shokudo Vegan** (organic, entirely plant-based Japanese comfort food sets, vegan cheeses, and desserts).
  * *Dinner:* **Mercy Vegan Factory** (plant-based wraps, burgers, and comfort bites).

#### Day 7 (Oct 7): Retro Osaka & Departure
* **Morning:** Explore the retro, bohemian neighborhood of **Nakazakicho**—a residential quarter filled with pre-war wooden buildings turned into independent art cafes.
* **Afternoon:** Visit **Umeda Sky Building** for panoramic views, or pick up souvenirs and tax-free gifts in the massive department stores around Osaka Station.
* **Evening:** 
  * Pick up stored luggage by 19:30.
  * Take the **JR Haruka Express** from Shin-Osaka or Tennoji straight to Kansai International Airport (KIX), roughly a 45–50 minute ride.
  * Arrive at KIX by 20:30–21:00 for your 23:30 flight.
* **Vegan Eats:**
  * *Farewell Lunch:* **Green Earth** (Osaka’s oldest vegetarian restaurant, serving plant-based lunch sets) or **Genmai Cafe**.
  * *Airport Dinner:* Food options inside KIX can be limited post-security for vegans; consider picking up a takeaway bento or konbini staples before arriving at the airport.

---

### Rail Logistics Tip
Instead of a national 7-day JR Pass (which saw a steep price hike and is no longer cost-effective for this route), **buy point-to-point Shinkansen tickets**:
1. Tokyo → Kyoto
2. Kyoto/Shin-Osaka → Hiroshima (Round-Trip)
3. Osaka → KIX (Haruka Express)

*You can book Shinkansen seats through the official **SmartEX** app/website or at station ticket machines.*
